name: example-write
description: The gated-write example: two local text files that exercise every write tier — a private notes file (loud, reversible, no gate), a simulated shared board (preview → --yes, or staged for `toolbelt approve`), and a destructive clear behind a typed-echo gate on /dev/tty (a --force that skips the word is honored only where /dev/tty opens)
hits: a local notes file + a simulated shared board
surface: CLI. Reads are free. `note add`/`note rm` touch only the operator's private file and run at once, printing their own undo. `board post` treats shared-board.txt as something other people see: at a terminal it previews and exits 0 until re-run with --yes; with no terminal (an agent) it stages the payload under ~/.local/share/exw/pending/ and reports `toolbelt approve example-write <code>`. `board clear` makes the operator type the word "clear" on /dev/tty; --force skips the word only where /dev/tty opens, never from a pipeline; there is no --yes. Every write prints an audit line to stderr and then re-reads the file and reports the diff.

origin.note: authored in this kit as the worked example of SENSIBILITIES #2. On win32 there is no /dev/tty: the typed-echo tier and approve degrade to refuse-and-tell (the file path to delete by hand, or the board post --yes command to type at a console); board post previews when stdin is a console and stages otherwise.

env.name: EXW_HOME
env.description: Where the two files and the pending/ staging dir live. Default ~/.local/share/exw. Tests point it at a temp dir.

auth.flow: none — local files under the operator's own home; no credential exists
auth.note: The staging queue ~/.local/share/exw/pending/ (dir 700, files 600, 15-minute expiry, single use) holds staged board posts awaiting terminal approval — payload text only, never a secret, so it is not an auth cache. Drop one with: toolbelt approve example-write --discard <code>

verbs.name: note add
verbs.note: private + reversible: loud flag, no gate — appends to the operator's own notes.txt and prints the exact `note rm <n>` that undoes it

verbs.name: note rm
verbs.note: private + reversible: loud flag, no gate — removes one line of notes.txt and prints the exact `note add` that restores it

verbs.name: board post
verbs.note: shared: preview by default (exit 0, nothing written), --yes executes, non-TTY stages for `toolbelt approve example-write <code>` where a human types yes on /dev/tty; --stage forces staging from a terminal

verbs.name: board clear
verbs.note: destructive: the operator types the word "clear" on /dev/tty after seeing the line count; --force skips the word only where /dev/tty opens (from a pipeline: exit 4 with the one command to run); --yes is a usage error

verbs.name: approve
verbs.note: what `toolbelt approve example-write` runs: shows the staged payload, takes a typed yes on /dev/tty, replays the exact board post in-process once, deletes the record; no terminal → refuse, never re-stage

safeguards: Tiers are a table in the code (VERBS in exw.mjs) and the test suite asserts the manifest's verbs[] matches it, so the contract and the behaviour cannot drift apart silently
note add / note rm touch only ~/.local/share/exw/notes.txt, a private file; they run without a gate but never quietly — each prints the file, the line delta, and the exact command that undoes it

board post never writes on a bare invocation: at a terminal it prints the exact bytes that would land and the --yes re-run, then exits 0; --yes is honored because refusing a deliberate post only pushes the work to an unguarded path

board post with no controlling terminal and no --yes stages the payload to ~/.local/share/exw/pending/<code>.json (dir 700, file 600, O_EXCL, 6-char [a-z0-9] code, 15-minute expiry, pruned on every touch) and exits 3 with `toolbelt approve example-write <code>`; nothing is written until a human confirms

approve opens /dev/tty — never stdin — shows the full staged payload, requires a typed yes, replays the exact staged arguments in-process through a one-shot module-level approval that no env var, flag, or stdin can set, and deletes the record whether or not the write succeeded (single use); with no terminal it refuses (exit 4) and never re-stages or auto-approves

board clear is gated by a /dev/tty typed-echo: the operator sees the line count and types the word "clear" back — "y", "yes", "Clear" and Enter all abort; piping into stdin cannot satisfy it because the gate opens the controlling terminal directly; there is no --yes

--force on board clear skips the typed word and is honored only when /dev/tty can be opened (harm reduction: a deliberate human is never refused); from a pipeline it exits 4 with the one command a human should run, because a flag an agent could have supplied is not evidence a human meant it. The terminal test is about the harness, not the caller — a process that inherits the operator's terminal passes it — which is why CLAUDE.md forbids an agent to pass --force itself

On win32, where /dev/tty does not exist, the typed-echo and approve gates refuse and tell (the file path to delete by hand; the --yes command to type at a console) rather than accept a console stdin a spawner could feed; this is declared here and in CLAUDE.md, not hidden
Every prompt states what it does, why the gate exists, and what yes and no each mean; the default is always no and no never changes a file (SENSIBILITIES #2)
--explain on note add, note rm, board post and board clear prints the plan — file, line delta, tier, gate — and writes nothing (SENSIBILITIES #5)

Every write prints an audit line to stderr (timestamp, verb, target, byte and line delta) and then RE-READS the file from disk and reports the diff, marking RE-READ MISMATCH if the expected change is not there: a successful write call is a claim, the re-read is the evidence (SENSIBILITIES #7, #2)

Files are created 600 and the data dir 700 under the operator's home; the staged record holds the post text only — this tool has no credential and the staging code has no field for one (SENSIBILITIES #11)

smoke_test.command: node exw.mjs list && node exw.mjs board post hello --explain && node --test test/exw.test.mjs
smoke_test.expect: list renders both files (empty is fine); the --explain pre-flight prints the plan and writes nothing; unit tests green — tiering, preview, staging record format, typed-echo parsing, approve replay

risk.worst_case: the two local files under ~/.local/share/exw are cleared — nothing outside the operator's home
